title: Tamsin and the Semester
premise: Oscar Dunmore has spent four years at Ashgrove Academy keeping his head down, but the senior college essay prompt—'What will you refuse to inherit?'—cracks him open. His answers, read aloud by mistake in class, expose the Founders' Ledger, a secret scholarship fund that has quietly bound the town's poorest students to the academy's wealthiest families for a century. Tamsin Vey, the headmaster's daughter and keeper of the ledger, becomes his reluctant ally as they race to reform the tradition before the board can bury it—and before graduation erases them both. In the end, Oscar chooses to stay one more year to rebuild the fund honestly, while Tamsin leaves for college carrying the truth instead of the secret.
about_author: Odile Galloway is the pen name of a former boarding school teacher who spent a decade listening to scholarship kids describe the strange arithmetic of gratitude and debt. She writes from a converted chapel on the coast, where she keeps her own ledger of stories students told her in confidence.

chapters.title: The Counting Days
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Opening week of senior year; Oscar catalogs his exit strategy—grades, recommendations, silence. A small humiliation at assembly establishes his invisibility. Emotional beat: weary resignation disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: One Honest Question
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. English teacher Ms. Ferro assigns the essay prompt 'What will you refuse to inherit?' Oscar writes three pages he never intends to submit. Emotional beat: the first crack in his armor, written in private.

chapters.title: Tamsin Vey Reads Aloud
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. A filing error puts Oscar's draft in the class reading pile; Tamsin, assigned to read anonymously, recognizes his handwriting. Emotional beat: mortification curdling into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Keeps the Books
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We learn she inherited custodianship of the Founders' Ledger from her late mother—a record of who owes whom. She approaches Oscar with a warning, not an apology. Emotional beat: guarded mutual recognition.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Tamsin shows him entries: his own name, his tuition quietly underwritten by the Halloway family since freshman year. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of everything he believed about earning his place.

chapters.title: Debt of Gratitude
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He confronts Mr. Halloway at the family's mill office and is offered a 'clean' continuation—plus a quiet expectation of loyalty. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into anger.

chapters.title: Tradition Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The academy's centennial gala celebrates the scholarship program as pure charity. Oscar and Tamsin watch the town toast its own mythology. Emotional beat: loneliness inside a crowd, and the first real conversation between them afterward.

chapters.title: Terms of Alliance
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She proposes they audit the ledger together—not to destroy it, but to make it honest. Her father suspects nothing yet. Emotional beat: cautious trust, sealed over cold coffee in the archive.

chapters.title: Names in the Margins
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They discover erased names—students pushed out when debts went unpaid, including Tamsin's mother's best friend. Emotional beat: grief for people neither of them ever met.

chapters.title: Ms. Ferro's File
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Their English teacher reveals she was a ledger student herself and points them toward the board minutes locked in the headmaster's study. Emotional beat: unexpected adult allyship, and fear of what it costs her.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Study
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A midnight break-in yields the minutes—and nearly gets them caught by Tamsin's father. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration braided together; the point of no return.

chapters.title: What Refusal Costs
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Her father confronts her privately, revealing he knew about the ledger all along and chose continuity over conscience. Emotional beat: love and duty pulling in opposite directions within one family.

chapters.title: Rumors and Ruin
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. An anonymous leak threatens Oscar's scholarship directly; classmates turn wary, and his acceptance letter hangs in the balance. Emotional beat: isolation, testing whether the alliance holds under pressure.

chapters.title: The Mill Closes Early
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Halloways retaliate economically against Oscar's mother's workplace. He considers signing their silence agreement. Emotional beat: temptation of safety versus the cost of complicity.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She photocopies the entire ledger and mails copies to every named family, detonating the secret on her own terms. Emotional beat: liberation laced with dread—she has burned her inheritance to save it.

chapters.title: Board Emergency
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The board convenes to expel them both; alumni descendants arrive furious or grateful in equal measure. Oscar speaks the essay aloud as testimony. Emotional beat: the invisible boy made visible, voice shaking and steady.

chapters.title: Vote
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The board deadlocks; Ms. Ferro and the town's small-business owners force a public review. Tamsin's father abstains—the closest thing to surrender he can manage. Emotional beat: exhausted hope, not yet victory.

chapters.title: Winter Term Reckoning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The academy agrees to convert the fund into transparent, need-based scholarships—but only if a student trustee oversees it. Every eye turns to Oscar. Emotional beat: the weight of being asked to stay.

chapters.title: The Essay, Revised
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He rewrites his college essay: what he refuses to inherit is the silence, not the school. He defers enrollment one year. Emotional beat: choosing a burden freely is the opposite of serving a sentence.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Father and daughter reach an uneasy peace over her mother's ledger; he gives her the original to take away. Emotional beat: forgiveness without absolution, tenderness without pretense.

chapters.title: Commencement
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At graduation, the new charter is announced publicly; Oscar crosses the stage to applause that finally feels earned. Tamsin watches from the faculty row, leaving tomorrow. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph, love acknowledged but unclaimed.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Split epilogue POV. Oscar unpacks boxes in the new student-trustee office; Tamsin sends him the first page of her own honest essay from college. Emotional beat: two inheritances remade—memory kept, duty transformed, love deferred but alive.
